meta.title: Weekly marketing report
meta.titleTag: Decidr — Weekly Marketing Report · 27 Jul – 2 Aug 2026

highlight.html: Quiet week — no new SQLs, spend winding down; the story is a firmographic split in the State of AI campaign. 98 new contacts (86 subscribers + 12 non-subscriber), 7 MQL+, 6 opportunities (all sales-created), and no new marketing SQLs. Paid social drove 53 contacts — all still subscriber-stage (the State of AI 2026 Report qualifying tail is expected next week, as we saw with the July launch). DecidrOS was silent (0 contacts). The standout finding: LinkedIn's State of AI leads are far larger companies than Meta's — 90% at 200+ employees (median 1k–5k) vs Meta's 19% (median 1–20). LinkedIn is the enterprise/ICP channel; Meta drives SMB volume.

sqlByProduct.note: MQL+ by product. All 6 marketing-qualified+ this week are Unassigned — the 6 sales-created opportunities (no product tag). Partnerships 1 MQL; DecidrOS had no contacts at all; Sugarworks 1 lead. No product-attributed SQLs this week.

stateOfAiSize.verdict: LinkedIn pulls far larger companies. 90% of LinkedIn's State of AI leads are 200+ employees (median 1k–5k) vs just 19% on Meta (median 1–20). LinkedIn is the enterprise/ICP channel; Meta drives SMB volume. If the 250+ employee ICP is the priority, weight State-of-AI budget toward LinkedIn.

observations.html: NEW — LinkedIn pulls enterprise, Meta pulls SMB. On the State of AI campaign, 90% of LinkedIn leads are 200+ employees (median 1k–5k) vs 19% on Meta (median 1–20). If the 250+ employee ICP is the target, LinkedIn is the channel to scale — Meta is efficient for volume but sub-ICP.

Coalescing filled 100% of the size data. company_size alone is ~1% populated, but combining it with total_number_of_employees and the LinkedIn domain-verified count filled all 42 State-of-AI leads. Standardising on the LinkedIn-verified field would make this repeatable every week.

Quiet week, no marketing SQLs. 98 contacts (86 subscribers), 7 MQL+, 6 opportunities — all sales-created. Paid social (53) is entirely subscriber-stage; expect the State of AI qualifying tail next week.
DecidrOS was silent. 0 DecidrOS contacts this week — with AI Roadmap off and no replacement demand engine, the DecidrOS top-of-funnel has stalled. Worth prioritising a new DecidrOS-specific campaign.

Spend winding down again — $3,331. Meta $2,006, LinkedIn $1,101, Google $223 — the lowest paid week in the series. Combined with 0 paid MQL, efficiency can't be judged until the State of AI tail lands.
All 6 opportunities were sales-created. Yoko Okano, Mike Montgomery, Bethany Mah, Bill Herman, Niosha Kayhani, Matt Hanrahan — via CRM/extension, none marketing-sourced or product-tagged.
